intended_object: The class of faithfully flat morphisms in the category of affine test objects, i.e. the opposite of the category of finitely generated commutative K-algebras: a morphism given by a K-algebra map B → A is in the class iff B → A is faithfully flat, so that Spec A → Spec B is flat and surjective. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation (single faithfully flat covers in Milne's descent argument) and the file's use of it.
explanation: A morphism f : X ⟶ Y in (FGAlgCat K)ᵒᵖ has f.unop : Y.unop ⟶ X.unop, and the body requires the underlying ring map Y.unop → X.unop to satisfy Mathlib's RingHom.FaithfullyFlat. So X's algebra is faithfully flat over Y's, the correct direction for Spec X → Spec Y to be a cover. The file confirms this through flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff and by proving the class contains identities, is closed under composition, and is stable under base change. The docstring's remark that the target algebra is finitely generated holds automatically, since every object of FGAlgCat K is of finite type. The property is Mathlib's general RingHom.FaithfullyFlat, applied to the specific test category (finite-type algebras over any commutative ring K). That category is the content of the definition, since it is the setting of the library's Milne-style results, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no class of morphisms on this category, only the ring-map property RingHom.FaithfullyFlat that the definition uses.
